text:
Sam W.: Follow-up from the private endpoint RFC. Saw a couple of customer reports where cert renewals fail because CP is logically separated from tenant VPCs. Wanted to sketch a resilient off-network renewal pattern and call out tradeoffs.

Maria L.: TL;DR? Is this the case where agents can't reach the signing service during maintenance windows?

Sam W.: Exactly. Two constraints we need to satisfy: (1) CP keeps CA keys (HSM/KMS), (2) tenants can run in "no inbound CP" mode (no CP-initiated connections).

Jin K.: We should avoid any design requiring customer-side KMS access or long-lived CP credentials inside the tenant. Security team: strong veto there.

Devon R.: Ops concern: when a rollout causes a control plane partition, we must avoid thousands of agents hammering artifact stores with CSRs. CSR stampedes = paging.

Sam W.: Proposed design (preferred): presigned CSR upload + CP signing worker (pull model). Flow: on onboarding CP creates a short-lived presigned upload URL for CSR and a presigned download URL for the signed cert. Agent generates CSR locally, uploads CSR to tenant object store using presigned upload. CP signing worker (running in CP) polls tenant artifact paths, picks up CSRs in batches, signs using CA in HSM, writes signed cert to presigned download path. Agent polls download path with jitter/backoff.

Jin K.: Why presigned vs tokens? Presigned URLs avoid storing tokens long-term on agents and reduce credential rotation complexity. But presigned URLs need single-use semantics and TTLs.

Maria L.: TTL and revocation tradeoffs: if we issue 24h certs, revocation is simple (wait max TTL) but renewal churn rises. If we go shorter, we increase load. We need telemetry to tune TTL per workload.

Devon R.: To mitigate CSR storms: agent-side rate limiter + randomized backoff window on startup and renewals. CP signing worker should batch sign (e.g., sign up to 250 CSRs per worker loop) and use parallel signing threads to reduce latency.

Sam W.: Minimal agent pseudocode: 
```
# agent renewal
if exists_local_cert_valid(): continue
csr = gen_csr()
upload_presigned(csr_url, csr)
for i in range(max_attempts):
  cert = http_get(presigned_download_url)
  if cert: install(cert); break
  sleep(jittered_backoff())
# if still no cert, install self-signed short-lived and emit alert
```

Jin K.: CP worker sketch: poll tenant prefix every 30s, collect CSR files, dedupe by agent-id, sign in a pool, write certs to the download path, mark CSR processed (move/delete). Add signing metadata: signer-id, signing-time, policy-version.

Maria L.: Auditability is mandatory. Signed cert metadata must include CP instance fingerprint and policy ID so revocation/forensics can trace origin. Also emit events to our audit log stream.

Devon R.: For customers that require minimal latency for renewals, offer an opt-in "in-VPC signer": ephemeral, attested signing instance that runs in customer VPC and holds ephemeral signing keys provisioned by CP on demand. This is opt-in and involves attestation, lifetime limits, and HSM-backed signing. Heavy but necessary for some compliance.

Sam W.: Revoke strategy: prefer short cert TTL by default (24h) + ability to immediately blacklist via a revocation endpoint consumed by our gateways. Implement CRL-like list but treat it as advisory; rely primarily on short TTL to reduce blast radius.

Jin K.: Metrics we need: renew_success_rate, mean_time_to_rotate, fallback_self_signed_percent, csr_queue_depth, signer_latency_p50/p95. These feed alerts/Optimize suggestions.

Maria L.: Operator runbook: (1) identify sustained CSR queue growth -> scale signer workers; (2) if many agents on self-signed fallback -> identify CP connectivity regression; (3) revoke compromised certs by adding tenant to revocation list and accelerate TTL.

Devon R.: Implementation checklist: artifact API (presign endpoints + single-use semantics), signing worker with batch+parallel sign and HSM integration, agent library for presigned uploads + jitter/backoff, console UI for cert state + alerts, audit log schema + signer tagging.

ops-bot: Infra job scheduled: artifacts-service/presign-endpoints -> canary deploy 2026-04-02T01:00Z.

Sam W.: Next: I'll draft a concise RFC addendum that prefers presigned CSR upload + CP signing worker as default, documents optional in-VPC signer, and includes runbook and metrics. Any objections?

Maria L.: +1 to presigned default. Add appendix for TTL tuning per workload.

Jin K.: +1. I'll prototype the signer worker and share perf numbers for batch sizes.

Devon R.: +1. Make sure signing worker logs signer identity and policy id in audit stream.

Sam W.: Thanks all 609. I'll open the addendum and ping for reviews.
